note: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the evidence-tier breakdown quoted as the system's single most-cited honesty number. Keyed by OracleKind (engine/crucible/framework/v2/verify/models.py) — the detector-kind registry; the drift guard (docs/tests/test_coverage_tiers_drift.py) asserts this file lists EXACTLY the OracleKind members and that every evidence-branches.json oracle_version is one of them, so the tier vocabulary can never reference a detector the engine does not have or omit one it does. `tier` is a CLOSED vocabulary describing the STRONGEST evidence a detector kind has ever judged: `external` (real bytes from a third-party system on the internet), `own_infrastructure` (real infrastructure the system builds and destroys), `local` (real bytes over a real connection/process on the testing machine — crediting the in-process cloud simulator, the convention 05-weakness-types.md states it uses), `fixtures` (only hand-written evidence). Note fact-capability and tier are ORTHOGONAL: a branch may be fact_capable yet its detector tiered `fixtures` because no live/local exercise has run. Regenerate the doc blocks with `python3 docs/capability-matrix/gen_coverage_tiers.py`.

tiers.label: Outside system
tiers.meaning: Real bytes from a third-party system on the public internet.

tiers.label: Own infrastructure
tiers.meaning: Real bytes from infrastructure the system builds, uses and destroys.

tiers.label: Real local process
tiers.meaning: Real bytes over a real connection or process on the testing machine.

tiers.label: Retained source code
tiers.meaning: Re-derived from retained source-code bytes by a static re-parse — no live process, no runtime observation.

tiers.label: Fixtures only
tiers.meaning: Only ever judged evidence a person wrote by hand.

detectors.name: Session fixation

detectors.name: MFA bypass
detectors.evidence: Real local process — the loopback benchmark app over a real connection; under a fail-closed operator attestation, a PRIVATE-READ REDUCTION proves a factor-1-only session read a post-MFA-gated victim datum (the factor-2-enforcing twin produces nothing)

detectors.name: Password-reset token invariant
detectors.evidence: Real local process — the loopback benchmark app over a real connection; a P2-bound PRIVATE-READ REDUCTION proves a consumed reset token is reusable, a predictable arithmetic-counter token collision, or (via the password_reset_cross_user private-read differential) a token issued to one principal reads another principal's private datum — a byte-identical token across account labels stays a LEAD (labels never prove distinct principals), and the single-use-expiring, distinct-random, and secure deterministic twins produce nothing

detectors.name: Escalation primitive
detectors.evidence: Fixtures only — and permanently so by design, as explained above

detectors.name: CSP permissive-policy posture
detectors.evidence: Fixtures only — a retained-header parse (the effective script-src) that re-derives the permissive weakness offline; the sibling of clickjacking/csrf/postMessage posture

detectors.name: Static source-code rule
detectors.evidence: Retained source code — the SAST bridge re-parses the retained source region (Python ast) and re-derives a CODE PROPERTY, never runtime exploitability; three tiers are FACT-capable (a broken-crypto invocation, an insecure-flag literal, or a direct intra-procedural taint) and insecure-randomness is a recognised detection pointer that stays a LEAD (fail-closed, never a FACT — needs crypto-provenance dataflow); a non-Python or unparseable region REFUSES
